description: A representation, omission or practice was made to consumers (FTC Act §5 deception, element 1).
The representation, omission or practice is likely to mislead a consumer acting reasonably (element 2).
The representation, omission or practice is material to the consumer's decision (element 3).
Material terms of a negative-option/auto-renewal offer must be clearly and conspicuously disclosed before obtaining billing information.
Express informed consent must be obtained before charging the consumer.
A simple mechanism to stop recurring charges must be provided.
Total price including mandatory fees must be shown up front, not added late in checkout (drip-pricing / junk-fee rules, e.g. FTC Rule on Unfair or Deceptive Fees, state analogues).
False or fabricated urgency/scarcity claims (timers that reset, static stock counts) are deceptive practices.
